issues.title: raw_counts counts every tick_trade row in the session windows with no product/instrument filter, so other products' rows show as mismatches
issues.why: raw_counts filters tick_trade only by ts_event against the session windows, while ledger_totals is filtered by the product's shape. _session_row takes the union of instrument keys from both maps, so any instrument with raw rows but no shape ledger row becomes a Mismatch(ledger 0, raw n) and coverage exits 3. This is the case's known bug, fixed later in 459ac7bd.

issues.title: caught_up is evaluated (and can read 'yes') when a tier and start are set but the wanted end is unknown
issues.why: _product_status sets wanted=None when _wanted_end returns None (no entry.end and no tick_dataset_edge row), so _scope covers only held sessions, yet line 217 passes wanted=wanted_start is not None, which is True. caught_up then returns all(...) over held sessions only (vacuously True with none), so status prints 'caught up: yes' beside 'edge: never observed', against the slice's 'without a wanted range: n/a'. Latent while ES has tier=None, but reachable once a tier is set on a database with no edge row (for example one rebuilt by ingest alone); the later 8a9c47ec fix kept the same wanted flag.

issues.title: Coverage reads ledger totals and raw counts in separate autocommit snapshots, so an ingest committing between them gives a false mismatch
issues.why: _connect opens the read connection with autocommit=True, and build_coverage runs session_verdicts, ledger_totals and raw_counts as separate statements with no enclosing transaction. Ingest commits a unit's tick_trade rows and ledger rows together, so a commit landing between the ledger_totals and raw_counts statements leaves raw > ledger for that session and coverage exits 3 reporting corruption. The window is real but transient and clears on rerun, so it is worth a REPEATABLE READ fix but does not block merge.

issues.title: raw_counts' range join against unnested sessions may cost rows x sessions with no ts_event index; the cost is unmeasured
issues.why: tick_trade is a hypertable on ts_event created with create_default_indexes => FALSE and its key leads with instrument_id, so the outer WHERE bound gives chunk exclusion but the BETWEEN join to unnest has no index and will likely be a nested loop with a join filter evaluated rows x sessions times. Whether that is materially slow on realistic ranges is not settled by the code; the slice design chose this exact join. An EXPLAIN ANALYZE of coverage over a multi-month ES range on production-sized data would settle it.

issues.title: calendar_sessions misses psycopg_pool PoolTimeout, so a calendar outage escapes as a traceback
issues.why: psycopg_pool defines PoolTimeout (and PoolClosed) as subclasses of psycopg.OperationalError, so the existing except (psycopg.OperationalError, CalendarNotFoundError) catches it and maps it to TickCalendarError, which exit_code_for maps to exit 4. The claimed traceback cannot happen.

issues.title: An out-of-calendar-range --start/--end exits 4 (storage), which the read epilog does not describe; unreachable-calendar path untested
issues.why: calendar_sessions turns OutOfPopulatedRangeError into TickCalendarError, which exit_code_for maps to EXIT_STORAGE, while READ_EPILOG names exit 4 only for an unreachable database. The message is still printed, so the effect is a misclassified exit code for an input/range problem (later changed to exit 1 in 3188a92f); the second bullet's pool-exception doubt is unfounded since PoolTimeout is an OperationalError.

issues.title: age() renders negative ages (clock skew) as '-1d 23h'
issues.why: age() applies floor divmod to int(seconds), so a negative input yields days=-1, hours=23 and prints '-1d 23h'. A negative age needs the status host's clock to lag the pass host's; the effect is a cosmetic line in human output only.

issues.title: build_coverage itself does not reject end <= start
issues.why: The only caller at head, the CLI, rejects end <= start before calling build_coverage. The unguarded path matters only for a future API caller (slice 230), so this is hardening against input that cannot arrive today.

issues.title: calendar_sessions duplicates product_session_days' calendar open/error-mapping/close
issues.why: calendar_sessions repeats the same TradingCalendar open, the same exception-to-TickCalendarError mapping and close as tick_calendar.product_session_days. True duplication, but both copies behave identically today; a DRY refactor, not a defect.

issues.title: status_reads re-declares the unit/request join instead of using manifest_reads.UNIT_FROM
issues.why: _UNITS is the same string as manifest_reads.UNIT_FROM, and status_reads adds SQL on tick_request/tick_archive_unit outside the modules manifest_reads' docstring names. Structure and DRY only; no behavior difference.

issues.title: Unannotated SQL fragments in status_reads may fail strict pyright's LiteralString check
issues.why: The project's type checker is mypy, not pyright (pyproject says so explicitly), and mypy treats LiteralString as str, so these str constants do not produce a merge-blocking error. The fragments are unchanged at the current HEAD, consistent with the check passing.

issues.title: Wanted-range/tier path of status (caught_up, holed, tier rendering) has no integration test
issues.why: Every integration test uses TICK_UNIVERSE[0], which has tier=None, so _wanted_end, the wanted branch of _scope and caught_up True/False are not exercised end to end. A test gap; the defect it would catch is graded separately.

issues.title: Render branches and age() in tick_status_render have no direct tests
issues.why: No test imports tick_status_render, and the CLI tests cover only the tier-less, edge-less path. Missing tests for paths that are otherwise correct (apart from the cosmetic negative-age case graded separately).

issues.title: _session_row rescans all ledger/raw keys per session (quadratic) synchronously
issues.why: Each _session_row builds the instrument set by scanning every key of both dicts, so assembly is O(sessions x keys). This is a one-shot CLI with no concurrent tasks on its loop, and the cost is small next to the tick_trade scan for the same range; no real effect.

issues.title: Module-level assert guards that _BUCKET_ROWS covers every TickSessionStatus
issues.why: The exhaustiveness check is a bare module-level assert, stripped under -O. The same pattern already exists in tick_exit.py; a missing bucket would only drop a row from human output. Style/hardening.

issues.title: run_mapped's per-verb storage tuple splits exit-code policy from tick_exit.exit_code_for
issues.why: run_mapped checks the caller's storage tuple before exit_code_for so read verbs map TickDatabaseUnreachable to 4 while writers keep 1. Behavior is correct and tested; this is a design-cohesion point.

issues.title: _product_status and _product_lines are long and mix responsibilities; jsonable lives in the status module
issues.why: Function length and module placement concerns only; no behavior effect.

issues.title: shape_units is queried twice per product, and spread filtering uses list membership
issues.why: _scope and session_verdicts each call shape_units for the same shape, and contracts are filtered with 'c not in spreads'. Both true; one extra manifest query and a small quadratic over a handful of contracts have no real effect.

issues.title: _read and the coverage read callback type the connection as Any
issues.why: _read takes Callable[[Any, str], ...] and the inner read uses conn: Any although manifest_reads defines Conn. Typing looseness only.
